clue.text: Place for two different kinds of course

definitions.text: Place for two different kinds of course

parts.words: Place for two different kinds of course
parts.note: a Kent town famous for its championship golf links, and also the name of a study course that alternates college with work placements

explanation.surface: A venue that offers two contrasting courses of study or dining.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kent town is home to Royal St George's golf course, and a course that alternates classroom terms with time in industry takes the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a Kent town with a famous golf course whose name also labels a work-and-study course.

clue.text: Money paid to a king's retainers

definitions.text: Money paid to a king's retainers

parts.words: Money paid to a king's retainers
parts.note: the retainers are not loyal servants but kidnappers who are holding the king, and the money buys his release

explanation.surface: Wages handed out to a monarch's household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retainers' suggests servants on the payroll; here it means captors retaining the king, and the phrase 'a king's ransom' adds to the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: money demanded by captors for releasing a prisoner, here a captured monarch.

definitions.meaning: a tubular pasta, eaten as food
an 18th-century English fop who affected Continental, especially Italian, fashions

explanation.surface: A dish suited to a fashionable Italian gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: In 18th-century Britain young men back from the Grand Tour who dressed in extravagant Italian style were called by the same name as the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a familiar pasta, and an old name for a fop who affected Italian fashion.

definitions.meaning: a particular is an individual item or point
a small group of soldiers given a special task

explanation.surface: A fussy description of some troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a single item of information, and a squad of troops assigned to a duty.

clue.text: Divine healer has disturbed a bishop, perhaps

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a bishop is one example of a chess man

explanation.surface: A holy healer has upset a senior clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges HAS into SHA; the bishop is not a clergyman but a chess piece, a MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal priest who heals through contact with spirits, hence a divine healer.

clue.text: Plenty of fish in a circle

definitions.meaning: a large group of fish swimming together
a group of people sharing ideas or a style, as a set of artists or thinkers

explanation.surface: Lots of fish swimming round in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a shoal of fish, and a group of like-minded thinkers or artists.

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: Dad owns a circular plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow round dish used in ancient Roman libations is called by this name.

indicators.note: disposed badly, so the letters of the two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone as unfriendly and grumpy as they always are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-disposed' reads as a second synonym beside 'Hostile', but it signals the anagram of AS EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is a hostile attitude towards it.

parts.note: lots are not abundance but the numbered items put up at a sale

explanation.surface: Generous people with plenty to give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' reads as 'a great deal'; at a sale room a lot is an item for bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: people who conduct sales offer items called lots to bidders.

indicators.note: hordes at war are in confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An island once overrun by fighting tribes.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Greek Dodecanese islands.

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
lines of goods are a shop's wares

explanation.surface: Without warning a young woman acquires some poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' suggests verse or telephone lines; in commerce a line is a range of products for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken unawares means caught suddenly and without warning.

indicators.note: the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A springtime celebration falling during the school break.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu festival of colours, celebrated in spring.

parts.note: Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009
less means without, as in penniless

explanation.surface: Things remain unchanged in the absence of the national poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poet Laureate is the official national poet in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary and not moving at all is what still means here.

indicators.note: compiling puts material together in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scholars of faith who put together collections of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars of divinity are experts in religion.

clue.text: Perhaps it's Norma Hill who answers the call

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini, one example
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A woman called Norma Hill picks up the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma Hill looks like a person's name; Norma is Bellini's opera and a tor is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone switchboard worker answers calls and puts them through.

parts.note: a French gold twenty-franc piece named after the emperor whose regime minted it

explanation.surface: Money struck by the person it is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a French gold coin named for the emperor under whom it was minted.

definitions.meaning: to take another's words, as if on loan

explanation.surface: Was a Victorian novelist guilty of copying?
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the surname of the Victorian writer George, and taking someone else's material.

parts.note: the trio of female detectives in the TV series named after their unseen boss Charlie; the word's Greek root means messengers

explanation.surface: A trio of couriers working for Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly messengers share their name with the three detectives in the series Charlie's Angels.

clue.text: Obstruction caused when two nerves fuse

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck means nerve in the sense of cheek or effrontery

explanation.surface: A blockage occurs where two nerve fibres join together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nerves' suggests anatomy; both pieces are slang for nerve as boldness, and 'fuse' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point that holds up traffic or progress is an obstruction.

definitions.meaning: to take on or grapple with an opponent or problem
a ship's ropes and pulleys as a set of gear

explanation.surface: Get involved with the ropes on a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to take on a task or opponent, and a ship's ropes and pulley gear.

clue.text: It's put on to get warm

definitions.text: It's put on to get warm

parts.words: It's put on to get warm
parts.note: not a coat or jumper but a vessel switched on to heat water

explanation.surface: A garment one wears to warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' suggests clothing; in Britain you put this on to boil water for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a household vessel switched on so its water heats up.

clue.text: A shop in Edinburgh stocking wood

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer as a shop stocks goods

explanation.surface: A Scottish store selling timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer whose timber is a common softwood.

parts.note: a three-piece suite is a sofa plus two padded seats with rests for the elbows

explanation.surface: The cosy section of a set of furniture or rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: one of the padded seats in a three-piece suite of furniture.

clue.text: Counter magazine for women in Turkey

indicators.note: the magazine goes inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey
Elle is a women's fashion magazine

explanation.surface: A sales stand for a ladies' magazine in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop counter; it is a person who counts, such as a bank clerk or vote counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who counts votes or a bank cashier is a counter.

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: willowy means slender and lissom

explanation.surface: A girl named Sally is nearly graceful.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a name; a sallow or sally is a type of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally, also called sallow, is a kind of low-growing tree of this family.

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide away, so the answer is tucked inside the two words

explanation.surface: Every oyster produces certain substances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secrete' suggests oysters producing pearl; it means conceal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixtures of metals are made of component elements; the clue loosely calls them components.
